subject: [ACTION REQUIRED] Error budget release gate (WARN-ONLY) rolling out this week
related_links: Confluence: Release gates using error budgets (eng-platform how-to)
PR: redwood#18463 (release gate step queries budget status + override token mechanism)
body:
From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, Feb 8, 2026 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: [ACTION REQUIRED] Error budget release gate (WARN-ONLY) rolling out this week

Team —

We’re rolling out the new error budget release gate step in CI/CD this week in WARN-ONLY mode.

What this is
- A deploy pipeline step that queries the control plane “budget-check” endpoint for the scoped service + tier (Hosted vs Dedicated) and returns a status.
- In WARN-ONLY, it will NOT block deploys. It will annotate the CI output and post a short summary to the deploy log so we can validate correctness before we turn on soft-block.

Where this will show up (starting Tue/Wed depending on repo)
- redwood/control-plane deploy pipelines (all envs)
- API gateway and routing pipelines (pilot services only)

What you’ll see
- Gate output includes:
  - Scope: {service} / {tier} / {region (if applicable)}
  - Status: OK | AT_RISK | EXHAUSTED | UNKNOWN
  - Budget remaining (%), burn-rate (short + long windows), and evaluation timestamp

How to interpret results
- OK: budget burn is within policy thresholds; no action.
- AT_RISK: budget burn is elevated; release is still allowed in warn-only, but please double-check canary and consider smaller blast radius (flagged rollout, smaller canary).
- EXHAUSTED: service/tier budget is depleted for the policy window; in warn-only this is informational, but this is the scenario that will block once we flip to soft-block.
- UNKNOWN: gate could not compute a decision (e.g., missing data, budget job delayed, mis-scoped labels). Treat UNKNOWN as a signal to report (see below).

What I need from you / your teams
1) Please do NOT ignore warnings this week. If you see AT_RISK/EXHAUSTED on a routine deploy when everything looks healthy, that’s a potential false positive we need to fix before enforcement.
2) When you hit a warning that doesn’t match your understanding of system health, please reply in-thread or forward to me with:
   - CI run URL
   - Service name + tier (Hosted/Dedicated)
   - Approx time + region
   - Whether the deploy was a no-op / doc-only / config-only (helps with correlation)

Known footguns we’re watching closely
- Tier propagation gaps (request context not consistently tagging metrics across gateway → routing → runtime)
- Streaming endpoints: latency SLI (TTFT vs full duration) still being tuned; warnings may be noisy on chat/completions routes
- 499/timeout classification: we’ve seen mismatches between logs and metrics in a few places; treat these as “likely false positive” until verified

Next steps / timeline
- This week: validate correctness + noise levels (warn-only)
- Next: soft-block for pilot services only (Ethan + Sean to sign off once false positives are down)
- Hard-block: not scheduled until we have stable SLI attribution and a clean override path

Thanks — this is the piece that makes budgets “felt” in day-to-day engineering, so catching bad signals early matters.

- Ethan

Ethan Park
Engineering Manager, Control Plane
Redwood Inference


---

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, Feb 8, 2026 at 10:04 AM PST
Subject: Re: [ACTION REQUIRED] Error budget release gate (WARN-ONLY) rolling out this week

Thanks Ethan.

Two clarifications so I can set expectations with oncall/SRE:

1) What does the gate do if it can’t reach the budget-check endpoint / times out? Does UNKNOWN still return success (since warn-only), or is it a hard failure of the pipeline step?

2) For Dedicated: are we scoping by customer pool or just by tier/service for the pilot? I want to avoid a situation where one noisy customer view makes a general Dedicated gate “look red” for everyone.

Also, can you confirm whether the gate output is already linking to the dashboard/runbook? Even in warn-only, we’ll want folks to land in the right place quickly.

- Sean

Sean Gallagher
Director, Site Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference


---

From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, Feb 8, 2026 at 11:03 AM PST
Subject: Re: [ACTION REQUIRED] Error budget release gate (WARN-ONLY) rolling out this week

Good questions.

1) Budget-check unreachable / timeout
- In warn-only, the step will NOT fail the pipeline.
- We currently return UNKNOWN with a reason (e.g., "budget_check_timeout" / "budget_service_unavailable") and print a one-liner asking to report the CI URL.
- When we move to soft-block, we’re leaning toward “fail-open” (do not block) for infrastructure errors, but “fail-closed” for explicit EXHAUSTED. We’ll finalize that policy with SRE before the flip.

2) Dedicated scoping
- For the pilot we are NOT doing per-customer pool gating.
- Scope is {service} + {tier=Dedicated} + {region} where available.
- Dedicated pool readiness SLIs will still page/ticket per customer views separately; we’re keeping the release gate coarse initially to avoid leaking or coupling to customer-specific noise.

3) Links to dashboards/runbook
- Yes. Gate output includes:
  - SLO dashboard link (pre-filtered to service/tier)
  - Error budget policy page link
  - “Error budget exhaustion response” runbook link
- If anyone sees missing/incorrect links in the output, please flag it (same info: CI run URL + which repo/pipeline).

I’ll drop a short snippet in #eng-platform tomorrow with an example of the gate output so folks know what to look for.

- Ethan
